headline: G MINING VENTURES POSTS $2,555/OZ MARGIN in Q1 — Record Gold Price Unlocks New Era for Junior Producers
snippet: G Mining Ventures (TSX:GMIN) produced 31,846 ounces of payable gold in Q1 at its Tocantinzinho Mine in Brazil, realising $4,143/oz against an AISC of $1,588/oz — a margin of roughly $2,555 per ounce that would have been unthinkable just three years ago. Full-year guidance of 160,000–190,000 ounces remains unchanged, illustrating how producers with locked-in cost structures are seeing extraordinary operating leverage at current gold prices.

headline: US Partners Deploy COLORADO SCHOOL OF MINES Tech at the Highest-Grade Rare Earth Deposit in America
snippet: US Critical Materials Corp. and Bayan Mining and Minerals have signed a strategic MOU to deploy proprietary Colorado School of Mines processing technology at Montana's Sheep Creek Project, described as the highest-grade validated rare earth deposit in the United States and hosting light and heavy REEs plus gallium, scandium, and yttrium. The collaboration directly targets a domestic US processing pathway for AI-critical minerals, timed ahead of this week's Trump-Xi summit where rare earth trade restrictions are a central agenda item.

headline: FIRST MAJESTIC Posts Largest-Ever Dividend as Revenue Jumps 95% — Silver at $87 Triggers Record Margins
snippet: First Majestic Silver (TSX:AG) reported Q1 2026 revenue of $477 million — up 95% year-on-year — as operating margins expanded fourfold to $52 per silver ounce equivalent, driven by the sustained rally above $85/oz; the company declared its largest-ever quarterly dividend of $0.0171 per share. Production totalled 3.5 million silver ounces, 34,341 gold ounces, and meaningful zinc, lead, and copper by-products across its Mexican and US operations.

headline: 7 G/T GOLD, 1,780 G/T SILVER in Best Hit: Mithril Extends Copalquin Resource 300m Beyond Known Boundary
snippet: Mithril Silver & Gold (TSXV:MSG / ASX:MTH) hit 7.00 g/t gold and 370 g/t silver over 9.65 metres at Copalquin's Target 1 in Durango, Mexico, including a best 0.5m interval of 30.7 g/t Au and 1,780 g/t Ag — confirming high-grade mineralisation approximately 300 metres west of the current resource boundary. Results support a meaningful footprint expansion ahead of a June 2026 mineral resource estimate update within a 25,000-metre drill campaign still underway.

headline: 26.9% ANTIMONY at 495m Depth: Bald Hill Assays Confirm Wide High-Grade Zones in New Brunswick Critical Mineral Play
snippet: Antimony Resources (CSE:ATMY) returned grades of 26.9% and 6.9% antimony from the latest drill assays at the Bald Hill deposit in New Brunswick, with wide mineralised intercepts extending to 495 metres depth and an ongoing 19,000-metre Phase 2 program targeting a conceptual 2.7 million tonne resource at 3–4% Sb. Antimony's designation as a US-Canadian critical mineral for battery storage, military munitions, and semiconductors has attracted sustained investor attention to the Bald Hill system.

headline: HELIOSTAR METALS Logs Record $30.9M Mine Earnings in Q1 — Junior Gold Producers Join the Bull Market Bonanza
snippet: Heliostar Metals reported record Q1 2026 mine operating earnings of $30.9 million and net income of $14.0 million on gold production of 11,743 ounces and 43,798 silver ounces, with an AISC of $1,996/oz against realised prices well above $4,000/oz. The result signals that junior gold producers — not just majors — are capturing extraordinary margin expansion as the gold price settles into its post-$5,589 correction range.

headline: TRUMP-XI SUMMIT: China's RARE EARTH CARD Looms Large Over Critical Minerals Trade Negotiations
snippet: As Trump and Xi convene their first direct summit, China's rare earth and critical mineral export restrictions are emerging as Beijing's primary bargaining chip, with analysts warning that the terms of any deal could redraw the global mining investment map for a decade. China released a draft of its MIIT enforcement framework two weeks ahead of the summit — a signal that supply leverage is being held in reserve for the negotiating table.

headline: Royalty Deal Sealed on Sunnyside COPPER-SILVER Project in Arizona — Royalty Market Heats Up Around US Copper
snippet: Evolve Royalties has signed a binding letter of intent to acquire a royalty on Barksdale Resources' Sunnyside copper-silver project in Arizona, as the royalty financing market increasingly bets on US copper at record prices. Barksdale is currently running a Phase II drill program at Sunnyside's Triple C porphyry target with assays returning intervals of 0.93% copper over 60.96 metres.

headline: China Imported 790+ TONNES of Silver in Early 2026 — Solar Explosion Fuels Fifth Straight Structural Deficit Year
snippet: Frank Holmes' weekly Gold SWOT analysis for U.S. Global Investors highlights China importing more than 790 tonnes of silver in early 2026, a pace driven almost entirely by explosive solar panel manufacturing growth as Beijing pushes its green energy buildout. The data reinforces the structural deficit thesis: global silver supply fell short of demand by more than 148 million ounces last year, the fifth consecutive annual shortfall, and mine production growth shows no sign of keeping pace.

headline: CAMECO HALTS KEY LAKE MILL After Saskatchewan Bridge Collapse — 2026 Uranium Production Guidance in Jeopardy
snippet: A bridge collapse on the Smoothstone River — Cameco's primary supply route to its northern Saskatchewan operations — has halted milling at Key Lake and reduced mining activity at McArthur River, the world's highest-grade uranium mine, after flooding severed deliveries of critical operating materials. Cameco has warned that its 2026 McArthur River/Key Lake production guidance is at risk depending on how long road restrictions persist, with no timeline for resumption given.
